s: After Stephen describes his vision, the crowd throws him out of the city and stones him. The witnesses lay their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul. Stephen calls on the Lord Jesus to receive his spirit, kneels, asks that the sin not be held against them, and falls asleep.

l: The Acts of the Apostles, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 8
s: A great persecution scatters the assembly in Jerusalem, with Saul ravaging it and dragging men and women to prison, while the scattered believers preach the word. Philip proclaims Christ in Samaria, where signs and healings bring great joy and many are baptized, including the sorcerer Simon. Peter and John come from Jerusalem, pray for the Samaritans, and lay hands on them so they receive the Holy Spirit; when Simon offers money for this power, Peter rebukes him and tells him to repent, and Simon asks for prayer. Directed by an angel and the Spirit, Philip meets an Ethiopian eunuch reading Isaiah on the road toward Gaza, explains the passage as being about Jesus, and baptizes him. The Spirit then catches Philip away, the eunuch goes on rejoicing, and Philip is found at Azotus and preaches in the cities until he reaches Caesarea.

l: Paul, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 8
s: Saul consented to Stephen's death. He ravaged the assembly, entering every house and dragging men and women off to prison.

l: assembly in Jerusalem, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 8
s: The assembly in Jerusalem suffered a great persecution and was scattered throughout Judea and Samaria, except for the apostles. Its scattered members went around preaching the word.

l: disciples (believers gathered at Pentecost), The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 8
s: A great persecution arose against the assembly in Jerusalem on the day of Stephen's burial. Saul entered houses and imprisoned men and women, and the believers were scattered throughout Judea and Samaria, which led them to preach the word wherever they went.

l: Philip, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 8
s: Philip went down to Samaria, proclaimed Christ, and did signs, including casting out unclean spirits and healing the paralyzed and lame. Guided by an angel and the Spirit, he met the Ethiopian eunuch, explained Isaiah to him starting from the Scripture he was reading, and baptized him. The Spirit then caught him away, and he was found at Azotus, preaching in the cities until he came to Caesarea.

l: Samaria, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 8
s: Samaria received Philip's preaching of Christ, and there was great joy in the city. The apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God and sent Peter and John there.

l: Samaritans, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 8
s: The Samaritans listened with one accord to Philip, and men and women believed and were baptized. They received the Holy Spirit when Peter and John prayed and laid hands on them, and Peter and John later preached the Good News in many Samaritan villages. Earlier they had listened to Simon the sorcerer and called him the great power of God.

l: Jerusalem, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 8
s: Jerusalem was where the persecution arose and where the apostles remained while others were scattered. The apostles there sent Peter and John to Samaria, and the two returned to Jerusalem afterward. The Ethiopian eunuch had come to Jerusalem to worship, and Philip was sent to the road going down from it to Gaza.

l: Jesus, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 8
s: Philip proclaimed Jesus Christ to the Samaritans, along with good news about God's Kingdom and his name. The Samaritans had been baptized in his name, and Philip preached about Jesus to the eunuch starting from the Isaiah passage.

l: God, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 8
s: God's Kingdom was part of the good news Philip preached in Samaria. Peter told Simon that the gift of God cannot be obtained with money and that Simon's heart was not right before God, urging him to ask God for forgiveness.

l: Holy Spirit, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 8
s: The Holy Spirit had not yet fallen on any of the Samaritan believers, who had only been baptized in the name of Christ Jesus. They received him when Peter and John prayed and laid hands on them, and Simon sought to buy this power. The Spirit also told Philip to join the eunuch's chariot and then caught Philip away after the baptism.

l: Simon, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 8
s: Simon was a sorcerer who amazed the people of Samaria and was called the great power of God. He believed and was baptized, stayed with Philip, and was amazed by the signs. He then offered the apostles money for the power to give the Holy Spirit; Peter rebuked him, called him in the poison of bitterness and bondage of iniquity, and told him to repent, and Simon asked Peter to pray for him.

l: Peter, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 8
s: Peter was sent with John from Jerusalem to Samaria, where they prayed for the believers and laid hands on them to receive the Holy Spirit. He sharply rebuked Simon for trying to buy the gift of God, told him to repent, and afterward returned to Jerusalem preaching in many Samaritan villages.

l: Ethiopian eunuch, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 8
s: The Ethiopian eunuch was a man of great authority under Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was over all her treasure. Returning from worship in Jerusalem, he was reading Isaiah in his chariot and asked Philip to explain it. After hearing about Jesus he was baptized and went on his way rejoicing.

l: Isaiah passage, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 8
s: The eunuch was reading a passage from Isaiah about one led like a sheep to slaughter, silent like a lamb before its shearer, whose judgment was taken away and whose life is taken from the earth. The eunuch asked whether the prophet meant himself or someone else, and Philip, beginning from this Scripture, preached Jesus to him.

l: The Acts of the Apostles, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 9
s: Saul, breathing threats against the Lord's disciples, sets out for Damascus with authority from the high priest to bind followers of the Way. On the road a light and the voice of Jesus stop him and leave him blind; Ananias, sent by the Lord, lays hands on him, he regains sight, is baptized, and begins proclaiming Jesus in the synagogues. The Jews plot to kill him, so his disciples lower him over the wall in a basket, and in Jerusalem Barnabas brings him to the apostles after the disciples fear him. When the Hellenists seek to kill him, the brothers send him off to Tarsus, and the assemblies enjoy peace. Peter then heals the paralyzed Aeneas at Lydda and raises Tabitha (Dorcas) at Joppa, where he stays with Simon the tanner.

l: Paul, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 9
s: Saul, breathing threats and slaughter, sought letters to bring followers of the Way bound to Jerusalem, but was stopped near Damascus by a light and the voice of Jesus, was blinded for three days, and was healed and baptized. He then proclaimed Christ in the synagogues, confounded the Jews, escaped a plot by being lowered in a basket through the wall, and was brought by Barnabas to the apostles in Jerusalem. After the Hellenists sought to kill him, the brothers sent him to Tarsus.

l: Jesus, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 9
s: Jesus spoke from the light to Saul, identifying himself as the one Saul was persecuting and telling him to enter the city. He told Ananias in a vision that Saul was his chosen vessel to bear his name to the nations, kings and Israel, and that Saul would suffer for his name. Peter healed Aeneas and raised Tabitha in his name.

l: Ananias, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 9
s: Ananias, a disciple at Damascus, was told by the Lord in a vision to go to Saul on the street called Straight. He voiced concern about Saul's evil toward the saints but obeyed, laid hands on Saul, and told him he would receive sight and be filled with the Holy Spirit.

l: Peter, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 9
s: Peter traveled through the region and came to the saints at Lydda, where he healed Aeneas. He was called to Joppa, sent the mourners out, prayed, and raised Tabitha. He then stayed many days in Joppa with Simon, a tanner.

l: Barnabas, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 9
s: Barnabas took Saul, whom the disciples in Jerusalem feared, and brought him to the apostles. He told them how Saul had seen the Lord on the way, that the Lord spoke to him, and that he had preached boldly in Jesus' name at Damascus.

l: Aeneas, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 9
s: Aeneas, a man at Lydda, had been bedridden eight years from paralysis. Peter told him Jesus Christ heals him and to get up and make his bed, and he rose immediately, leading all who lived at Lydda and Sharon to turn to the Lord.

l: Tabitha, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 9
s: Tabitha, also called Dorcas, was a disciple at Joppa full of good works and acts of mercy; the widows showed the garments she had made. She became sick and died, and Peter told her to get up, and she opened her eyes and sat up alive.

l: Damascus, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 9
s: Damascus was Saul's destination to seize followers of the Way, and the place where he was healed, baptized, and first proclaimed Christ in the synagogues. The Jews there plotted to kill him and watched the gates, but he escaped over the wall in a basket.

l: Jerusalem, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 9
s: Jerusalem was where Saul intended to bring the bound disciples and where he had earlier made havoc of those who called on Jesus' name. After his conversion, the disciples there feared him until Barnabas brought him to the apostles, and he preached and disputed there until the Hellenists sought to kill him.

l: Lydda, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 9
s: Lydda was where Peter visited the saints and healed the paralyzed Aeneas. Its inhabitants, along with those of Sharon, turned to the Lord after seeing him. It was near Joppa, from which disciples sent for Peter.

l: Joppa, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 9
s: Joppa was the home of the disciple Tabitha, who died there and was raised by Peter in an upper room. The event became known throughout Joppa and many believed in the Lord. Peter stayed there many days with Simon the tanner.

l: the Way (disciples of the Lord), The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 9
s: Saul sought to bind followers of the Way, men or women, and bring them to Jerusalem. After his conversion the disciples at Damascus received him, while those in Jerusalem initially feared him. The assemblies throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria had peace, were built up, and multiplied in the fear of the Lord and the comfort of the Holy Spirit.

l: Jews, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 9
s: The Jews of Damascus were confounded by Saul's proof that Jesus is the Christ, and after many days conspired to kill him, watching the gates day and night. Their plot became known to Saul, who escaped.

l: Paul's vision on the road to Damascus, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 9
s: Near Damascus a light from the sky shone around Saul, he fell to the earth, and heard Jesus ask why he persecuted him. Jesus told him to enter the city to learn what to do, while his companions stood speechless, hearing the sound but seeing no one.

l: Saul's blindness and healing, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 9
s: Saul rose from the ground unable to see, was led by hand into Damascus, and went three days without sight, food or drink. Ananias laid hands on him, something like scales fell from his eyes, and he received sight, rose, and was baptized.

l: Tabitha's resurrection, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 9
s: After Tabitha died and was laid in an upper room, Peter was sent for and found the widows weeping. He sent everyone out, knelt and prayed, told her to get up, and presented her alive; many in Joppa believed in the Lord.

l: The Acts of the Apostles, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 10
s: Cornelius, a devout centurion in Caesarea, is told by an angel in a vision to send men to Joppa to fetch Simon Peter. Meanwhile Peter, hungry on a housetop, sees a sheet full of animals descend three times and is told by a voice to kill and eat, and that what God has cleansed he must not call unclean. The Spirit tells Peter to go with the three men sent by Cornelius, and he travels to Caesarea with some brothers from Joppa. There Peter tells the gathered household that God shows no favoritism and preaches about Jesus Christ, and the Holy Spirit falls on all who hear, including Gentiles. Peter then commands that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ, and they ask him to stay some days.

l: Cornelius, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 10
s: Cornelius is a centurion of the Italian Regiment in Caesarea, a devout God-fearing man who gives generously to the needy and prays always. After an angel's vision he sends two servants and a soldier to Joppa for Peter, gathers his relatives and close friends, and falls at Peter's feet in worship, which Peter refuses. He and his household hear Peter's message, receive the Holy Spirit, and are baptized.

l: Peter, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 10
s: Peter, also called Simon, is staying with a tanner named Simon in Joppa when he prays on the housetop, falls into a trance, and sees the sheet vision, at first objecting that he has never eaten anything common or unclean. Directed by the Spirit, he goes with Cornelius's men to Caesarea, declares that God has shown him not to call any man unholy or unclean, and preaches about Jesus. When the Spirit falls on the hearers, he asks whether anyone can forbid their baptism and commands that they be baptized.

l: God, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 10
s: God sends an angel to Cornelius, shows Peter through the vision that he must not call unclean what God has cleansed, and has the Spirit send the three men to Peter. Peter learns that God shows no favoritism and accepts in every nation anyone who fears him and works righteousness. God anointed Jesus with the Holy Spirit and power, raised him the third day, and appointed him Judge of the living and the dead.

l: angel (sent to Cornelius), The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 10
s: An angel of God appears to Cornelius at about the ninth hour and says his prayers and gifts to the needy have gone up as a memorial before God. He tells Cornelius to send men to Joppa to get Simon, who is also called Peter, and says where he is staying, with a tanner named Simon by the sea. Cornelius later describes him as a man in bright clothing, and the visitors call him a holy angel.

l: Jesus, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 10
s: Peter describes Jesus Christ as Lord of all, who brought good news of peace, was from Nazareth, and was anointed by God with the Holy Spirit and power. He went about doing good and healing those oppressed by the devil, was killed by hanging on a tree, and was raised by God on the third day and shown to chosen witnesses who ate and drank with him. He is appointed Judge of the living and the dead, all the prophets testify that everyone who believes in his name receives remission of sins, and the new believers are baptized in his name.

l: Holy Spirit, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 10
s: The Spirit tells Peter that three men are seeking him and to go with them without doubting, since the Spirit has sent them. While Peter is still speaking in Cornelius's house, the Holy Spirit falls on all who hear the word. The circumcised believers with Peter are amazed that the gift was poured out on Gentiles, who speak in other languages and magnify God.

l: vision of the sheet (Peter's vision), The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 10
s: While Peter prays on the housetop around noon, he sees heaven opened and a great sheet let down by four corners, holding all kinds of four-footed animals, wild animals, reptiles, and birds. A voice tells him to rise, kill and eat, and says that what God has cleansed he must not call unclean. This happens three times before the sheet is taken up into heaven, and Peter is perplexed until Cornelius's men arrive; he later applies it to people, saying he should call no man unholy or unclean.

l: Gentiles, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 10
s: Cornelius and the household gathered with him in Caesarea are Gentiles, whom Peter, a Jew, would normally consider unlawful to visit or join himself to. They listen to Peter's message, and the Holy Spirit is poured out on them, with the gift evidenced by their speaking in other languages and magnifying God. Peter then commands that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ.

l: clean and unclean (dietary and social), The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 10
s: Peter declares in the vision that he has never eaten anything common or unclean, but the voice answers that what God has cleansed he must not call unclean. Peter explains in Caesarea that it is unlawful for a Jew to join himself to or visit one of another nation, but that God has shown him he should call no man unholy or unclean. The distinction is thus extended from foods to people.

l: Peter's sermon, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 10
s: In Cornelius's house Peter opens by saying God shows no favoritism and accepts in every nation the one who fears him and works righteousness. He recounts the gospel of Jesus: his anointing, ministry of doing good and healing, death on a tree, resurrection on the third day, appearance to chosen witnesses, and appointment as Judge. He closes by saying all the prophets testify that everyone who believes in Jesus's name will receive remission of sins, and the Holy Spirit falls on the hearers while he is still speaking.

l: The Acts of the Apostles, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 11
s: Peter returns to Jerusalem, where those of the circumcision criticize him for entering and eating with uncircumcised men. Peter explains in order his vision at Joppa, the Spirit's instruction to go with the three men from Caesarea, the angel's message to the man in Caesarea, and the Holy Spirit falling on the Gentiles. The Jerusalem believers fall silent and glorify God for granting the Gentiles repentance to life. Meanwhile, scattered believers preach in Antioch, where many Hellenists believe, and the Jerusalem assembly sends Barnabas, who brings Saul from Tarsus; the disciples are first called Christians there. Agabus predicts a great famine, and the Antioch disciples send relief to the Judean brothers through Barnabas and Saul.

l: Peter, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 11
s: Peter goes up to Jerusalem and defends his visit to uncircumcised men by recounting his vision at Joppa, the Spirit's command, and the Holy Spirit falling on the Gentiles. He concludes that he could not withstand God, and his critics are silenced.

l: Gentiles, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 11
s: The Gentiles are reported to have received the word of God, and the Holy Spirit fell on them as it did on the apostles at the beginning. The Jerusalem believers conclude that God has granted them repentance to life.

l: those of the circumcision, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 11
s: Those of the circumcision contend with Peter in Jerusalem, objecting that he went in to uncircumcised men and ate with them. After hearing his account, they hold their peace and glorify God.

l: vision of the sheet (Peter's vision), The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 11
s: In a trance at Joppa, Peter saw a great sheet let down from heaven by four corners, containing four-footed animals, wild animals, creeping things, and birds. A voice told him to kill and eat, and after he refused, said not to call unclean what God has cleansed. This happened three times before everything was drawn back up to heaven.

l: God, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 11
s: God cleansed what Peter considered unclean and gave the Gentiles the same gift he gave the believing Jews. The Jerusalem believers glorify God for granting the Gentiles repentance to life.

l: Holy Spirit, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 11
s: The Spirit told Peter to go with the three men without discriminating, and the Holy Spirit fell on the Gentiles as Peter began to speak. Barnabas is described as full of the Holy Spirit, and Agabus indicates the coming famine by the Spirit.

l: Cornelius, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 11
s: The man in Caesarea, whose house Peter entered, reported that he had seen an angel standing in his house. The angel told him to send to Joppa for Simon called Peter, who would speak words by which he and all his house would be saved. The text does not name him in this chapter.

l: Jesus, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 11
s: Jesus Christ is the Lord in whom Peter and the others believed, and the Gentiles received the same gift when they believed. Believers from Cyprus and Cyrene preach the Lord Jesus to the Hellenists in Antioch.

l: scattered believers, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 11
s: Those scattered by the oppression that arose about Stephen travel to Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, at first speaking only to Jews. Some men of Cyprus and Cyrene then preach the Lord Jesus to the Hellenists in Antioch, and a great number believe.

l: Antioch, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 11
s: In Antioch, the Hellenists hear the Lord Jesus preached and a great number believe and turn to the Lord. Barnabas and Saul teach many people there for a year, and the disciples are first called Christians in Antioch. Prophets also come there from Jerusalem, and its disciples send relief to Judea.

l: Barnabas, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 11
s: Barnabas is sent by the Jerusalem assembly to Antioch, where he rejoices at God's grace and exhorts the believers to remain near the Lord. He is described as a good man full of the Holy Spirit and faith, fetches Saul from Tarsus, and later carries relief to Judea with him.

l: Paul, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 11
s: Barnabas goes to Tarsus to look for Saul, finds him, and brings him to Antioch. They teach many people there for a year, and Saul then helps carry relief to the elders in Judea.

l: the Way (disciples of the Lord), The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 11
s: The disciples are first called Christians in Antioch. As each has means, they determine to send relief to the brothers in Judea.

l: famine, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 11
s: Agabus, one of the prophets who came from Jerusalem to Antioch, indicates by the Spirit that a great famine will come over all the world. It happens in the days of Claudius.

l: relief for the brothers in Judea, The Acts of the Apostles, Chapter 11
s: Each Antioch disciple, according to their means, determines to send relief to the brothers living in Judea. They do so, sending it to the elders by the hands of Barnabas and Saul.
